- scripts/render_prompt.sh | Line or code reference: inject_identity_recall_block — text.split("\n\n", 1)
  Problem: The function splits rendered prompt text at the first double-newline and injects the identity block between the two halves. For mode prompts that start with a `# tier: ...` metadata line followed by a blank line (e.g. `prompts/mode-plan.txt`), that first double-newline occurs *before* the `Role: … Goal: …` paragraph, so the identity block is placed between the tier header and the actual opening paragraph instead of immediately after it. This means the model would see `<identity-recall>` before encountering the role/goal paragraph that describes what the identity refers to, defeating the compaction-recall intent.
  Why it fails at runtime: After context compaction the model re-emits the `<identity-recall>` block but it has already been separated from the role/goal paragraph by the blank line that was the original split point; on long prompts the injected block can end up far above the operational instructions, weakening recall reliability.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
